headline: Bank of Japan Raises Policy Rate to 1.25%, Highest in 31 Years
seoTitle: Bank of Japan Raises Rate to 1.25%, 31-Year High | FMB News
seoDescription: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25%, its highest level in 31 years, as it continues monetary-policy normalization.
deck: Japan’s central bank lifted its benchmark rate by 25 basis points in a 7-2 decision, extending a historic retreat from ultra-low monetary policy.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Bank of Japan raised its policy interest rate from 1.0% to 1.25% on September 18, the highest level in 31 years. Reuters and the Associated Press independently reported the decision. The BOJ board approved the increase by a 7-2 vote, with two members dissenting.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The 1.25% target and the 7-2 vote are independently confirmed by Reuters and AP. Reuters reported that Governor Kazuo Ueda said the bank’s policy focus has shifted toward preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its 2% target.

sections.heading: What remains developing
paragraphs: The path of further BOJ tightening remains unresolved. Reuters reported that the yen weakened after the decision as investors weighed the two dissenting votes and the pace of future increases. Future moves will depend on inflation, wages, the yen, energy costs and economic conditions.

sections.heading: Why it matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Japan is one of the Philippines’ largest trade, investment and development partners. A sustained shift in Japanese interest rates can affect the yen, regional capital flows and financing conditions. The direct effect on remittances, prices or Philippine households is not predetermined and depends on exchange rates and broader market conditions.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the yen, subsequent BOJ guidance, Japanese inflation and wage data, and whether higher Japanese rates alter regional funding conditions or investment flows into Southeast Asia.
